name: Establishing Closed Guard
description: Wrapping your legs around the opponent's waist with ankles crossed to control their posture and prevent passing. The foundational bottom guard position.

name: Armbar from Closed Guard
description: Isolating an arm, swinging a leg over the head, and extending the hips to hyperextend the elbow joint. A core fundamental submission.

name: Triangle Choke from Closed Guard
description: Trapping one arm and the head between the legs and squeezing to cut off blood flow through the carotid arteries with the opponent's own shoulder.

name: Kimura from Closed Guard
description: Using a figure-four grip on the wrist to torque the shoulder into internal rotation. Works as both a submission and a control/sweep entry.

name: Guillotine Choke from Closed Guard
description: Wrapping the neck from the front with the forearm against the throat and lifting to compress the airway or arteries.

name: Omoplata from Closed Guard
description: Using the legs to trap and rotate the opponent's shoulder while their arm is pinned, creating a shoulder lock with the hips.

name: Scissor Sweep
description: From closed or open guard, off-balancing the opponent while scissoring the legs to knock them over to one side and come up on top.

name: Hip Bump Sweep
description: Sitting up explosively and driving the hip into the opponent to knock them backward, ending in mount. Pairs naturally with the kimura.

name: Flower (Pendulum) Sweep
description: Swinging the leg like a pendulum while controlling an arm and the opponent's leg to roll them over the shoulder and come up into mount.

name: Open Guard Retention
description: Using framing, hip movement, and active feet to recover and maintain guard, preventing the opponent from passing the legs.

name: Butterfly Sweep
description: From butterfly guard, using an underhook and a hook behind the opponent's knee to elevate and roll them over to one side.

name: De La Riva Sweep
description: Using a De La Riva hook around the lead leg plus grips to off-balance the opponent backward and sweep or transition to the back.

name: Tripod Sweep
description: From open guard, pushing one ankle while hooking the other leg and pulling the arm to topple a standing opponent backward.

name: Establishing Half Guard
description: Trapping one of the opponent's legs between your own while fighting for an underhook to prevent the pass and create attacking angles.

name: Old School Sweep from Half Guard
description: From the underhook in half guard, grabbing the trapped-side ankle and driving into the opponent to come up and reverse the position.

name: Knee Slide (Knee Cut) Pass
description: Slicing a knee across the opponent's trapped thigh while controlling the upper body to slide into side control.

name: Toreando (Bullfighter) Pass
description: Pinning both of the opponent's legs to the mat by the knees and sprinting around to the side like a matador.

name: Stack Pass
description: Folding the opponent onto their shoulders by stacking their hips over their head, removing their leverage to walk around into side control.

name: Leg Drag Pass
description: Dragging one of the opponent's legs across the centerline and pinning it to nullify the guard, then settling into a dominant control.

name: Over-Under Pass
description: Controlling one leg with an overhook and the other with an underhook, then driving forward with head pressure to grind through the guard.

name: Double Under Pass
description: Scooping both arms under the opponent's thighs, stacking them, and driving forward to pass to side control.

name: Maintaining Side Control
description: Using crossface and underhook, hip pressure, and weight distribution to pin the opponent on their back and shut down escapes.

name: Americana from Side Control
description: Pinning the opponent's wrist to the mat and using a figure-four grip to crank the shoulder into external rotation. A classic beginner submission.

name: Kimura from Side Control
description: Isolating the far arm with a figure-four grip and rotating the shoulder into internal rotation for the lock.

name: Side Control to Mount Transition
description: Sliding a knee across the belly or stepping over the hips while controlling the upper body to advance from side control into the mount.

name: Maintaining Mount
description: Using grapevines, knee positioning, and upper-body control to stay heavy and balanced on top while defending bridges and elbow-escapes.

name: Armbar from Mount
description: Isolating an arm, climbing to a high mount, and spinning to swing a leg over the head to extend the elbow.

name: Americana from Mount
description: Pinning the wrist to the mat and applying a figure-four to torque the shoulder while mounted.

name: Arm Triangle from Mount
description: Trapping the opponent's arm against their own neck and using shoulder pressure plus a head-and-arm squeeze to cut off blood flow.

name: Establishing Back Control Hooks
description: Securing both heels inside the opponent's thighs (hooks) with a seatbelt grip to maintain the most dominant control position.

name: Rear Naked Choke
description: From the back, wrapping the arm around the throat and locking the grip to compress the carotids. The highest-percentage submission in BJJ.

name: Straight Ankle Lock
description: Trapping the foot in the armpit and applying pressure across the Achilles/ankle by extending the hips. The fundamental leg lock.

name: Kneebar
description: Isolating a leg and hyperextending the knee joint by driving the hips against it, similar in mechanic to an armbar for the leg.

name: Heel Hook
description: Controlling a leg entanglement and rotating the heel to torque the knee ligaments. A high-risk advanced submission requiring careful control.

name: Toe Hold
description: Using a figure-four grip on the foot to rotate the ankle and apply pressure to the ankle and knee.

name: Upa (Bridge and Roll) Mount Escape
description: Trapping an arm and same-side leg, then bridging explosively over the shoulder to roll the opponent off and end in their guard. The foundational mount escape.

name: Elbow-Knee (Shrimp) Mount Escape
description: Framing against the hips and shrimping to insert a knee and recover guard or half guard from under the mount.

name: Side Control Escape to Guard
description: Framing on the neck and hip and shrimping away to create space, then recovering full or half guard from underneath side control.

name: Side Control Escape via Underhook to Turtle
description: Winning the underhook from bottom side control and turning into the opponent to come up to the knees or turtle and reverse the pressure.

name: Rear Naked Choke Defense
description: Protecting the neck by tucking the chin and fighting the choking hand, then escaping the hooks to slide the hips down and turn into the opponent.

name: Posture and Break from Closed Guard (Top)
description: Maintaining straight posture with strong hand placement on the hips to resist attacks, then opening the legs to begin a pass.

name: Taking the Back from Turtle
description: From a turtled opponent, securing a seatbelt and inserting hooks to roll them and establish back control.

name: Turtle Recovery and Defense
description: Protecting the neck and hips while turtled, defending hook insertions, and looking to stand, recover guard, or roll out.

name: Double Leg Takedown
description: Changing levels, penetrating with a deep step, and driving through both legs to put the opponent on their back from standing.

name: Single Leg Takedown
description: Securing one leg and using angle changes and drives to finish the takedown from standing.

name: Knee on Belly Control
description: Placing a knee across the opponent's torso with the other foot posted, a mobile and heavy control that sets up submissions and transitions.

name: North-South Choke
description: From the north-south position, wrapping the arm under the neck and dropping shoulder pressure to compress the artery and airway.

name: Kimura Sweep from Half Guard
description: Trapping the arm in a kimura grip from bottom half guard and using it to off-balance and sweep the opponent to top position.

name: High Elbow Guillotine
description: A blood choke from the front headlock where you cinch the neck with the forearm blade high under the chin and lift the elbow, finishing without trapping an arm.

name: Arm-In Guillotine
description: A guillotine variation where the opponent's near arm is trapped inside the choke, compressing both the neck and shoulder for a powerful air/blood choke.

name: Low Elbow (Standard) Guillotine
description: The classic guillotine with the choking arm low across the throat, finishing by pulling up on the neck while driving the hips forward to crank the windpipe.

name: Marcelotine (High-Elbow No-Arm Guillotine)
description: Marcelo Garcia's high-elbow guillotine using a palm-to-palm or wrist grip with no arm trapped, finishing from guard by extending the hips and squeezing the elbow upward.

name: D'Arce Choke
description: A no-gi arm-triangle variant where the choking arm threads under the near arm and across the neck, with the hand reaching to the far bicep to compress the carotids.

name: Anaconda Choke
description: A front-headlock blood choke where you thread the arm under the neck and through the armpit, then roll to the side and gable-grip squeeze across the carotid.

name: Peruvian Necktie
description: A front-headlock choke where you secure a guillotine-style grip, sit back, and throw a leg over the opponent's neck to drive the head down and crank the choke.

name: Japanese Necktie
description: A mirror of the Peruvian necktie from the front headlock, throwing the leg over the back of the neck on the opposite side to apply a crushing neck crank/choke.

name: North-South Kimura
description: From north-south control, isolate the opponent's arm and apply a figure-four kimura grip, rotating the shoulder for the submission.

name: Arm Triangle from North-South
description: From north-south control, slide your arm under the near arm and across the neck, then walk to the near side and squeeze to compress the carotid with the opponent's own shoulder. A natural submission from the north-south pin.

name: Gogoplata
description: A choke from rubber guard or high guard where the shin is placed across the throat and the head is pulled down into it, compressing the windpipe.

name: Bulldog Choke
description: A standing or turtle front-headlock choke where you clamp the head against your chest with a tight headlock grip and squeeze to cut off the carotids.

name: Rear Triangle Choke
description: From back control, lock a triangle with the legs around the opponent's neck and one arm, finishing the blood choke from behind.

name: Side Triangle Choke
description: A triangle finished from a side-on angle, often transitioned from mount or side control, trapping the head and one arm between the legs.

name: Reverse Triangle Choke
description: A triangle applied facing the opposite direction (often from side control or an inverted position), with the legs locking around the neck and far arm.

name: Mounted Triangle
description: Transition from mount into a triangle by trapping one arm and swinging a leg over the head and shoulder, then finishing the choke off the back.

name: Arm Triangle (Kata Gatame) from Side Control
description: Trap the opponent's arm against their own neck and encircle the head, then walk to the far side and squeeze to compress the carotid with their shoulder.

name: Armbar from Back Control
description: From back control, isolate one arm and spin to attack the elbow joint with a straight armbar when the choke is defended.

name: Armbar from Side Control
description: From side control, trap the far arm and step over the head to spin into a straight armbar, extending the elbow against the hips.

name: Spinning Armbar from Guard
description: From closed or open guard, off-balance the opponent and spin underneath to swing a leg over the head and isolate the arm for the armbar.

name: Omoplata from Open Guard
description: Triangle the opponent's arm with your legs and rotate to apply a shoulder lock, controlling the hips to prevent the roll-out.

name: Wrist Lock from Closed Guard
description: Trap the opponent's hand against your body or chest and flex the wrist forward to attack the joint, often when they post inside your guard.

name: Bicep Slicer from Guard
description: Wedge your forearm or shin into the crook of the opponent's bent arm and lever it closed to compress the bicep and elbow.

name: Inside Heel Hook
description: From a leg entanglement like the saddle, control the heel and rotate it inward to torque the knee's ligaments; a high-finish-rate but dangerous submission.

name: Outside Heel Hook
description: From ashi garami or single-leg X, trap the foot and rotate the heel outward to apply rotational force to the knee.

name: Calf Slicer
description: Wedge your shin behind the opponent's knee and pull their lower leg toward you, compressing the calf muscle against your shin to attack the knee.

name: Estima Lock
description: A footlock variant where the foot is trapped flat against your hip/chest and the toes are driven down, applying intense pressure to the ankle and foot.

name: Aoki Lock (Inverted Heel Hook)
description: A bent-leg/inverted footlock attacking the ankle and Achilles, named after Shinya Aoki, applied by wrapping and torquing the lower leg.

name: Kneebar from Saddle
description: From the inside sankaku (saddle) entanglement, extend the opponent's leg and hyperextend the knee by bridging the hips against it.

name: Toe Hold from Ashi Garami
description: Grip the foot with a figure-four around the toes and rotate, applying combined ankle and knee torque from a leg entanglement.

name: Ashi Garami (Straight Ashi)
description: A foundational single-leg entanglement controlling one of the opponent's legs between yours, the launch point for straight ankle locks and heel hooks.

name: Single-Leg X Guard (SLX)
description: An entanglement where you control one of the opponent's legs with both of yours hooked around it, a strong base for sweeps and leg attacks.

name: X-Guard
description: A bottom open-guard position where you sit under the standing opponent with your legs crossed around one of their legs, off-balancing them for sweeps.

name: 50/50 Guard
description: A symmetrical leg entanglement where both players have one leg triangled around the other's, used for heel hooks and ankle locks by both sides.

name: Saddle (Inside Sankaku / 411)
description: A leg entanglement where the opponent's leg is triangled between your legs with their knee exposed inward, the dominant position for inside heel hooks.

name: Outside Ashi Garami
description: A leg entanglement controlling the leg with your outside hook, used to set up outside heel hooks and toe holds while limiting the opponent's rotation.

name: Body Lock Pass
description: Clamp both arms around the opponent's hips/lower back, pin their legs to the mat, and walk around to side control while denying any guard recovery.

name: Long Step Pass
description: From combat base or knee cut, step the trailing leg back and around in a long stride to clear the legs and circle to side control or the back.

name: Folding Pass
description: Stack the opponent by folding their knees toward their face, then circle around the folded legs to establish side control.

name: Smash Pass
description: Use a shoulder and hip pressure to flatten and crush one of the opponent's legs across their body, then walk around the smashed side to pass.

name: Headquarters (HQ) Position
description: A neutral passing position with one knee pinning the opponent's leg and combat base posture, from which you choose knee cut, leg drag, or back-step.

name: Back Step Pass
description: From headquarters, step the trailing leg backward over the opponent's legs to spin toward their hips and clear the legs for side control or back exposure.

name: X-Pass
description: Pin and cross the opponent's legs to one side with your arms, then jump or step to the open side and circle to side control.

name: X-Guard Sweep (Technical Stand-Up)
description: From X-guard, off-balance the opponent backward by extending your legs, then come up on top by following them and standing into a pass.

name: Single-Leg X Sweep
description: From single-leg X, extend your legs to break the opponent's base and follow them up to a top position or leg-lock entry.

name: Hook (Elevation) Sweep from Butterfly
description: From butterfly guard with an underhook, lift the opponent with your hook while falling to the side to send them over and come up on top.

name: Underhook Half Guard Sweep
description: From bottom half guard with a deep underhook, come to your side, take the back angle, and drive into the opponent to sweep them or take the back.

name: John Wayne Sweep
description: From half guard or X-guard, control the far leg and near hip and rotate to topple the opponent backward into a mounted or top position.

name: Sickle Sweep
description: From open guard with a foot on the hip and a hook behind the ankle, chop the leg out with a sickling motion to topple the opponent backward.

name: Lumberjack Sweep
description: Hug both of the standing opponent's legs/ankles and drive your shoulder forward to chop them down backward onto the mat.

name: Waiter Sweep (Deep Half)
description: From deep half guard, scoop under the opponent's far leg like carrying a tray and roll them over your body to come up on top.

name: Deep Half Guard
description: A bottom position where you burrow under the opponent's hips and control one leg deeply, used to off-balance and sweep heavier opponents.

name: Knee Shield Half Guard (Z-Guard)
description: A defensive half-guard frame placing a shin across the opponent's torso to create distance and set up sweeps, back takes, or recomposition.

name: Dogfight Position
description: A scrambling half-guard top/bottom position with both players on their knees fighting for the underhook, transitioning to sweeps or back takes.

name: Kimura Sweep from Closed Guard
description: Lock a kimura grip on the opponent's arm from guard and use it to off-balance them to the side, sweeping them over to come up in side control.

name: Arm Drag to Back
description: Grip the opponent's wrist and tricep and yank their arm across their body, exposing their back to take it from guard or seated positions.

name: Snap Down
description: From a collar tie, snap the opponent's head and neck downward to break their posture and expose the front headlock or back.

name: Ankle Pick
description: Use a collar tie or arm control to break posture, then drop and grab the opponent's ankle while driving their upper body to take them down.

name: High Crotch Takedown
description: Penetrate on a single leg high near the hip, lift, and finish by running the pipe or driving the opponent to the mat.

name: Body Lock Takedown
description: Clinch with both arms locked around the opponent's torso, break their balance, and trip or drive them to the ground while keeping the lock.

name: Back Control with Body Triangle
description: Maintain back control by triangling your legs around the opponent's torso, providing strong control to set up chokes without hooks being stripped.

name: S-Mount
description: A high-mount variation where your legs form an S-shape around the opponent's head and arm, ideal for isolating an arm for the armbar.

name: Technical Mount
description: A transitional mount where your knee is up beside the opponent's back as they turn, used to maintain control and take the back.

name: Crucifix
description: From the turtle or back, trap both of the opponent's arms (one with your legs, one with your arms), immobilizing them for chokes or strikes.

name: Twister
description: A spinal/neck crank from the truck position where you bend the opponent's body sideways by controlling the head and leg, originating from wrestling.

name: Truck Position
description: A lower-back-control entanglement trapping one of the opponent's legs with both of yours, the launch point for the twister and banana split.

name: Banana Split (Electric Chair)
description: From the truck or saddle, split the opponent's legs apart to attack the hip/groin with a crippling spread, often combined with leg control.

name: Berimbolo to Back
description: From a de la riva-style open guard, invert and roll underneath to spin to the opponent's back, taking hooks as they turn.

name: Granby Roll
description: A defensive shoulder roll used to recover guard or escape a turtle/pin by rotating your body underneath the pressure to free your hips.

name: Wrestle Up from Guard
description: From seated or open guard, attack the opponent's legs or use underhooks to stand up into a takedown or top position.

name: Back Escape (Scoot and Turn)
description: Defend the choke, slide your back down toward the mat to shuck off a hook, and turn into the opponent to escape back control to turtle or guard.

name: Guillotine Defense (Posture and Side)
description: Defend a guillotine by posturing up, dropping your chin, stacking your weight to the choking side, and circling your head out to relieve the pressure.

name: Triangle Defense (Posture and Stack)
description: Escape a triangle by posturing up, controlling the hips, and stacking your weight forward while pulling the trapped arm free.

name: Leg Lock Defense (Boot and Hide Heel)
description: Defend heel hooks and ankle locks by clearing the knee line, hiding the heel, pointing the toes, and rotating your knee toward the attacker.

name: Kneebar Defense
description: Defend a kneebar by bending your knee, rotating toward the attacker, and grabbing your own foot to relieve the hyperextension.

name: D'Arce / Anaconda Defense
description: Defend the D'Arce or anaconda by posturing the trapped arm, walking toward the attacker's head, and lowering your level to prevent the squeeze.

name: North-South Escape
description: Escape north-south control by framing on the hips, bridging, and shrimping to angle your body and recover guard or come to your knees.

name: Knee on Belly Escape
description: Escape knee-on-belly by framing on the knee, bridging to create space, and shrimping your hips out to recover guard.

name: Ghost Escape from Side Control
description: From bottom side control, frame and spin underneath the opponent toward their legs to escape out the back door and recover guard.

name: Heel Drag Mount Escape
description: From bottom mount, trap the opponent's foot, bridge, and roll over the trapped side to recover into their guard or half guard.

name: Guard Recovery (Shrimp and Frame)
description: Recover guard from inside the opponent's passing position by framing, shrimping your hips back, and inserting a knee or hook between you.

name: Front Headlock
description: Control the opponent's head and an arm from the front when their head is below their hips, the central hub for guillotines, D'Arce, and anaconda chokes.

name: Sprawl
description: Defend a takedown shot by throwing your legs back and dropping your hips onto the opponent's shoulders to flatten and stuff the attack.

name: Butterfly Guard
description: A seated open-guard position with both feet hooked inside the opponent's thighs, used to elevate and sweep them with hooks and underhooks.

name: Seated (Shin-to-Shin) Guard
description: A seated open guard where you control the opponent's lead leg with a shin-to-shin connection, used to enter X-guard, SLX, or arm drags.

name: No-Gi De La Riva Guard
description: An open guard hooking your leg around the outside of the opponent's lead leg while controlling the ankle, used for sweeps and back takes without grips.

name: Reverse De La Riva Guard
description: Hook your leg around the inside of the opponent's lead leg facing away, used defensively against knee-cut passes and to enter leg locks or sweeps.

name: Kimura Trap (Control System)
description: Secure a figure-four kimura grip and use it as a control to threaten the lock, sweep, or take the back depending on the opponent's reaction.

name: Reverse Americana
description: A keylock attacking the shoulder by bending the arm downward toward the hip rather than upward, used when the opponent's arm is pinned low.

name: Armbar from Mounted Triangle
description: When the mounted triangle stalls, switch to an armbar on the trapped arm by pivoting and extending the elbow over your hips.

name: Rear Naked Choke from Turtle Break
description: Break the opponent down from turtle, insert your hooks or take the back, and apply the rear naked choke around the exposed neck.

name: Straight Ankle Lock from Single-Leg X
description: From single-leg X, transition into ashi garami and apply a straight ankle lock (Achilles lock) by bridging into the trapped foot.

name: Dogbar (Inverted Kneebar)
description: An inverted leg attack hyperextending the knee from a rolled-under position, sometimes reached from 50/50 or saddle scrambles.

name: Z-Guard to Back Take
description: From knee-shield half guard, frame and underhook to climb to the opponent's back as they try to flatten the knee shield.

name: D'Arce from Half Guard Bottom
description: From bottom half guard, snake your arm under the opponent's neck and across to lock a D'Arce as a defensive-to-offensive transition.

name: North-South Position
description: A top control position where you face the opposite direction over the supine opponent, chest on their chest/face, controlling for chokes and transitions.

name: Monoplata
description: A one-legged shoulder lock similar to the omoplata but with a single leg over the arm, often hit from failed armbars or from mount.

name: Baratoplata
description: A shoulder lock from guard applying kimura-style rotation by wrapping your arm and leg around the opponent's arm, primarily from bottom open guard.

name: Guillotine Counter to Takedown
description: As the opponent shoots a takedown, catch a guillotine and pull guard or sweep, using the head control to either submit or reverse position.

name: Von Flue Choke
description: A shoulder-pressure choke applied as a counter to a guillotine attempt by driving your shoulder into the opponent's neck and walking toward their head.

name: Ninja Choke
description: A front-headlock blood choke similar to the anaconda but finished by sitting back and using a gable grip under the neck without rolling.

name: Standing Power Guillotine
description: Catch the head standing, lock a guillotine grip, and finish by arching back and pulling the neck up while squeezing, without going to the ground.

name: Pendulum (Hip Swing) Armbar from Guard
description: Use a pendulum swing of the legs to generate momentum and angle for finishing a tight armbar from the closed guard.

name: Leg Drag to Back Take
description: After dragging the opponent's leg across, follow the momentum to circle behind and take the back rather than settling in side control.

name: Tozi (Sao Paulo) Pass
description: From inside closed guard, control the opponent's hip with an underhook and drop your chest to drive forward and free your hips to pass.

name: Standing Closed Guard Break
description: Stand up inside the closed guard with strong posture and wedge a knee or elbow to pry the legs open and begin passing.

name: Kneeling Closed Guard Break (Sao Paulo / Log Split)
description: From the knees, posture up, drive an elbow inside the thigh, and split the legs apart to open and pass the closed guard.

name: Hip Switch (Float) Pass
description: While passing, switch your hips and float light on the opponent to follow their movement and prevent guard recovery on the way to side control.

name: Cross-Face Pressure Pass
description: Use a tight cross-face and shoulder pressure to turn the opponent's head away and flatten them while you walk around the legs to side control.

name: Single-Leg X to Kneebar
description: From single-leg X, extend and rotate to hyperextend the opponent's near knee when they posture to defend the sweep or ankle lock.

name: 50/50 Inside Heel Hook
description: From the 50/50 entanglement, expose and control the opponent's heel and rotate inward for a high-percentage inside heel hook.

name: Backside 50/50 (Outside Ashi Variant)
description: A modern leg entanglement controlling the leg from behind for a strong inside heel hook angle while limiting the opponent's escapes.

name: Matrix Leg Lock Entry
description: Enter a leg entanglement by inverting and threading your legs around the opponent's leg during a scramble or passing exchange.

name: Ashi Garami to Back Take
description: When the opponent rolls to defend a heel hook, follow the rotation and abandon the leg to climb to their back.

name: Imanari Roll
description: A rolling entry into a leg entanglement (typically the saddle) by diving and somersaulting toward the opponent's legs.

name: Butterfly Arm Drag to Back
description: From butterfly guard, arm drag the opponent across your body and follow to take the back as they fall forward.

name: Overhead (Balloon) Sweep from Butterfly
description: From butterfly or open guard, load the opponent onto your shins and throw them over your head with both feet to come up on top.

name: Tripod / Sickle Sweep Combination
description: Threaten the tripod sweep by pushing one leg; when the opponent steps to defend, switch to the sickle sweep on the other leg to topple them.

name: Ankle Lock as Pass Counter
description: As the opponent attempts to pass standing, drop into ashi garami on their lead leg and attack a straight ankle lock or heel hook.

name: Kimura to Back Take from North-South
description: Use a kimura grip from north-south to roll the opponent and follow to back control when they defend the shoulder lock.

name: Seatbelt Control from Back
description: Maintain back control with a seatbelt grip (one arm over the shoulder, one under the armpit) to prevent escapes and set up the rear naked choke.

name: Chair Sit Back Escape (Hand Fighting)
description: Defend the rear naked choke by hand-fighting the choking arm, dropping your hips to the mat, and sliding down to escape the back control.

name: Body Triangle Escape
description: Escape a back body triangle by controlling the top leg, posting, and turning your hips to break the lock and turn into the opponent.

name: Half Guard Recovery from Side Control
description: From bottom side control, frame and insert your knee to recover half guard as an intermediate step before recomposing full guard.

name: Bridge and Roll from Bottom Side Control
description: When the opponent overcommits weight, trap an arm, bridge explosively, and roll them over to reverse the position.

name: Wrist Lock from Side Control
description: Isolate the opponent's hand as they frame against you and flex the wrist to attack the joint from top side control.

name: Americana from Closed Guard
description: Trap the opponent's wrist to your chest and figure-four the arm to attack the shoulder with an upward keylock from the bottom.

name: Guillotine from Mount
description: When the bottom player turns to escape mount, wrap a guillotine around the neck and finish or use it to maintain control.

name: No-Gi Ezekiel (Sleeve-Free) from Mount
description: A no-gi Ezekiel using your own forearm and wrist across the throat from mount, sliding one arm behind the neck and choking with the blade of the wrist.

name: Arm Triangle from Guard (Top)
description: Catch the opponent's arm across their neck while passing or in their guard and lock the head-and-arm choke, finishing as you settle to the side.

name: Rolling Back Take from Turtle Top
description: From on top of a turtled opponent, secure a seatbelt and roll them over your shoulder to come up with back control and hooks.

name: No-Gi Clock Choke (Arm Version)
description: From the top of turtle, drive your forearm across the throat and walk around the head clock-wise to apply pressure to the neck without grips.

name: Guard Pull to Seated Guard
description: From standing, control the opponent and sit to your butt to establish a seated open guard rather than pulling closed guard.

name: Single Leg Finish (Run the Pipe)
description: After securing a single leg, run a circle toward the captured leg while driving to dump the opponent to the mat.

name: Duck Under
description: From a tie-up, lower your level and duck under the opponent's arm to take the back or a rear body lock for the takedown.

name: Russian Two-on-One to Back
description: Control the opponent's arm with a two-on-one Russian tie and circle behind to take the back or a body lock.

name: Guillotine on Sit-Up Escape
description: As the bottom player sits up to escape, snatch a high-elbow guillotine and pull guard to finish the choke.

name: D'Arce from Mount Transition
description: As the opponent turns to their side to escape mount, thread your arm under the neck and arm to lock a D'Arce choke.

name: Knee on Belly to Mount Transition
description: From knee-on-belly, step over the opponent's body to transition smoothly into mount while maintaining pressure.

name: Mount to Back Transition
description: When the bottom player turns to escape mount, follow them to technical mount and take the back with hooks and a seatbelt.

name: Leg Pummel into Ashi Garami
description: Pummel your leg inside the opponent's during open-guard exchanges to establish ashi garami and threaten leg attacks.

name: Outside Ashi to Saddle Transition
description: Transition from outside ashi garami to the saddle by stepping over and dropping your knee to access the inside heel hook.

name: 50/50 to Backside 50/50 Transition
description: Roll through from a neutral 50/50 to backside 50/50 to gain a dominant heel-exposure angle for the finish.

name: Guard Retention (Inversion and Leg Pummel)
description: Retain open guard against a pass by inverting, framing on the hips, and re-pummeling your legs back inside to re-establish the guard.

name: Knee Cut Counter (Underhook and Wrestle Up)
description: Counter the knee-cut pass by getting the underhook on the cutting side, blocking the hip, and coming up to wrestle back to neutral.

name: Toreando Pass Counter (Re-Hook)
description: Counter the toreando by following the pass direction and re-inserting a hook or De La Riva to recover open guard.

name: Omoplata to Back Take
description: When the opponent rolls to defend an omoplata, follow them and take the back instead of completing the shoulder lock.

name: Omoplata Sweep
description: Use the omoplata control to off-balance the opponent forward or to the side and come up on top into a passing or mounted position.

name: Hip Bump to Kimura Combination
description: Threaten the hip bump sweep; when the opponent posts their hand, trap it and attack the kimura as a combination.

name: Guillotine to Armbar Transition
description: When the guillotine is defended by posture, transition to an armbar on the same-side arm from guard.

name: Triangle to Armbar Transition
description: When the triangle is stalled, switch to an armbar on the trapped arm by adjusting your legs and hips.

name: Triangle to Omoplata Transition
description: Flow from a defended triangle into an omoplata by releasing the legs and rotating to attack the shoulder.

name: D'Arce to Anaconda Chain
description: Chain between the D'Arce and anaconda chokes from the front headlock depending on which side the opponent defends.

name: Guillotine to Anaconda Transition
description: When a guillotine is defended, transition the same arm position into an anaconda by threading through the armpit and rolling.

name: Rear Naked Choke (Arm-In Variation)
description: A rear naked choke finished with one of the opponent's arms trapped inside the choke, adding compression for the blood choke.

name: Short Choke (Hand-on-Head) from Back
description: A back-control blood choke where you place one hand behind the opponent's head and use the other arm's blade across the neck to finish without a full RNC.

name: X-Guard to Back Take
description: From X-guard, off-balance the opponent and climb up their leg to the back rather than sweeping to top.

name: Knee Shield to Old School Sweep Combo
description: From the knee shield, kick the shield to off-balance the opponent, then underhook and come up to sweep them.

name: Shin-to-Shin to X-Guard Entry
description: From the shin-to-shin guard, scoot under the opponent's leg to enter X-guard for sweeps and leg attacks.

name: Single-Leg X to X-Guard Transition
description: Transition between single-leg X and full X-guard depending on the opponent's base to maintain off-balancing control.

name: D'Arce from Bottom (Counter to Pass)
description: As the opponent attempts an over-under or smash pass and exposes their neck, lock a D'Arce from the bottom to submit them.

name: Kneebar from 50/50
description: From 50/50, isolate and extend the opponent's leg to hyperextend the knee as an alternative to the heel hook.

name: Toe Hold from 50/50
description: From 50/50, grip the foot in a figure-four and rotate for a toe hold when the heel hook is defended.

name: Leg Weave Pass
description: Thread your arm and shoulder through and over the opponent's legs to flatten and pin them while you walk to side control.

name: Float Pass to North-South
description: Stay light and float over the opponent's recovery attempts, circling toward their head to settle directly into north-south control.

name: D'Arce from Turtle Top
description: From the top of a turtled opponent, snake your arm under their neck and across to lock a D'Arce as you sit to the side.

name: Crucifix Neck Crank / Choke
description: From the crucifix, drive your forearm across the trapped opponent's neck to apply a crank or short choke while both their arms are immobilized.

name: RNC Defense (Two-Hand Peel)
description: Defend the rear naked choke before it sinks by gripping the choking arm with both hands, peeling it down, and protecting the neck while turning in.

name: Knee-Elbow Escape to Half Guard
description: From bottom mount, create space with elbow-knee framing and shrimp to extract a leg and recover half guard.

name: Armbar Defense (Hitchhiker Escape)
description: Escape an armbar by turning your thumb down (hitchhiker direction) and rolling toward the opponent's legs to free the arm.

name: Armbar Defense (Stack and Hide Hand)
description: Defend an armbar by clasping your hands, stacking your weight forward over the opponent, and stepping around to relieve the pressure and pass.

name: Kimura Defense (Grip Fight and Hide Hand)
description: Defend a kimura by gripping your own belt line or thigh, keeping the elbow tight, and turning into the opponent to relieve shoulder rotation.

name: Heel Hook Escape (Clear the Knee Line)
description: Escape a heel hook by spinning your knee toward the attacker (clearing the knee line) to neutralize the rotational pressure before the heel exposes.

name: Toe Hold Defense
description: Defend a toe hold by following the rotation and clearing your foot or grabbing the attacker's wrist to stop the figure-four torque.

name: Straight Ankle Lock Defense
description: Defend a straight ankle lock by sitting up toward the attacker, hiding the heel, and pushing their grip down off your foot.

name: Back Take from Side Control
description: From side control, when the opponent turns away to escape, follow them and insert your hooks to take the back.

name: High Mount Arm Isolation
description: Climb to high mount and pin the opponent's arms above the elbows to isolate one for an armbar or mounted attack.

name: Gift Wrap (Crossface Arm Trap)
description: From mount, trap one of the opponent's arms across their own face with a gift-wrap grip to control and set up the back take or choke.

name: Arm-In Guillotine to D'Arce Switch
description: When an arm-in guillotine stalls, release and switch the arm position to a D'Arce on the same side for a tighter finish.

name: Butterfly Half Guard to Back Take
description: From butterfly half guard with an underhook, elevate and rotate behind the opponent to take the back.

name: SLX Sweep to Leg Drag
description: From single-leg X, sweep the opponent and immediately leg drag to pass into side control or take the back.

name: K-Guard
description: A modern open-guard entanglement controlling the opponent's leg with your shin while inverting, used as an entry to leg locks and back takes.

name: K-Guard to Inside Heel Hook
description: From K-guard, enter the saddle by penetrating your legs and apply an inside heel hook on the controlled leg.

name: Ashi Garami to Kneebar
description: From straight ashi garami, transition by extending the leg and rotating your hips to attack a kneebar instead of the ankle lock.

name: Over-Under Pass to Back Take
description: From the over-under passing position, switch direction and circle to the back when the opponent turns to defend the pass.

name: Pull Guard Guillotine Finish
description: After catching a standing guillotine, jump or sit to closed guard and lock your legs to add hip extension power for the finish.

name: North-South to Armbar
description: From north-south, isolate an arm and swing into a spinning armbar by stepping over the head and extending the elbow.

name: Single Leg Defense (Limp Arm / Whizzer)
description: Defend a single leg by whizzering the attacking arm, pulling your leg out, and using the limp-arm to circle free and re-establish posture.

name: Double Leg Defense (Sprawl and Spin)
description: Defend a double leg by sprawling your hips down and spinning toward the back or front headlock to counter the takedown.

name: Turtle Defense (Hand Fight and Stand)
description: From turtle, hand-fight the front headlock, peel the grip, and explode back to your feet or recover guard before chokes set in.

name: Peruvian Necktie from Front Headlock
description: From a front headlock on a turtled opponent, secure the grip and sit to the side throwing a leg over the neck to apply the necktie.

name: Side Control to North-South Kimura Chain
description: Switch from side control to north-south to gain a better angle on the far arm, then attack the kimura.

name: Lockdown (Half Guard Control)
description: From bottom half guard, weave your legs to lockdown the opponent's leg, stretching them out to limit their pressure and set up sweeps.

name: Electric Chair Sweep
description: From the lockdown and an underhook, capture the opponent's leg and roll them backward, splitting their legs to sweep and threaten the groin stretch.

name: Plan B Back Take (from Lockdown)
description: From the lockdown with an overhook (whip-up), come up to take the opponent's back as they posture against the half guard.

name: Closed Guard Pull
description: From standing, grip the opponent's neck or body, sit, and lock your legs around their waist to establish closed guard from the feet.

name: Collar Tie and Underhook Clinch Control
description: Control the opponent's posture in the clinch with a collar tie and underhook to set up snap downs, takedowns, or the front headlock.

name: Double Underhooks Clinch Control
description: Secure double underhooks in the clinch to control the opponent's hips, set up body lock takedowns, or back takes.

name: Head and Arm Throw (No-Gi)
description: From an overhook and head control in the clinch, hip-toss the opponent over by loading them onto your hip without grips.

name: Guillotine Defense (Shoulder Pressure Counter)
description: When caught in a guillotine from the bottom, drive your shoulder into the neck, clear the choking arm and walk toward the head to escape the submission and pass.

name: RNC Finish Variations (Palm/Bicep)
description: Finish the rear naked choke by securing the choking-arm hand on the bicep and the other hand behind the head, then expanding the chest to compress the carotids.

name: S-Mount to Armbar
description: From S-mount, isolate the trapped arm and rotate back to extend the elbow for a high-control armbar finish.

name: D'Arce from Seated Guard (Counter to Forward Pressure)
description: From seated guard when the opponent drives their head down, snake the arm under their neck to lock a D'Arce and finish.

name: Funk Roll (Granby to Counter)
description: Use a wrestling funk roll from a defensive position to spin under the opponent and come up either in guard or on top.

name: Saddle Inside Heel Hook Finish
description: From the saddle, control the knee line and rotate the exposed heel inward with your forearm to finish the inside heel hook.

name: False Reap (Cross Ashi)
description: A leg entanglement crossing your outside leg over to expose the heel while keeping the knee line safe, used as a saddle alternative.

name: D'Arce Counter to Knee Cut
description: As the opponent knee-cuts and drops their head, catch a D'Arce from bottom to submit them during the pass attempt.

name: Kimura to Omoplata Chain from Guard
description: Threaten the kimura from closed guard; when the opponent defends by straightening the arm, transition to the omoplata.

name: Knee on Belly to Armbar
description: From knee-on-belly, when the opponent pushes your knee, trap the arm and spin into an armbar.

name: Back to Armbar (Choke Defense Counter)
description: When the opponent successfully defends the RNC by controlling your choking arm, spin off the back into an armbar on that arm.

name: X-Guard Off-Balance to Single Leg
description: From X-guard, off-balance the opponent and come up onto a single leg takedown for the sweep-to-top transition.

name: Knee Cut Directly to Mount
description: When the knee-cut pass meets little resistance, continue the cutting knee all the way across to settle directly into mount.

name: Anaconda from Sprawl
description: After sprawling on a takedown attempt, thread your arm under the opponent's neck and through the armpit and roll into an anaconda choke.

name: Guillotine from Sprawl
description: After sprawling on a shot, catch the guillotine on the lowered head and finish standing or by pulling guard.

name: Running Man Guard Recovery
description: Turn to your side and 'run' your bottom leg in a circular pedaling motion to keep your knee line in front of the passer, continuously re-facing them to prevent the pass.

name: Granby Roll Guard Recovery
description: As the opponent clears your legs to one side, roll over your shoulder (granby) to spin your hips underneath and re-insert your legs between you and the passer.

name: Hip Switch Guard Retention
description: Rotate your hips by switching the orientation of your legs and base foot, keeping your shins and knees pointed at the passer as they circle to either side.

name: Knee Shield Guard Retention
description: Keep a strong shin across the passer's chest or hip as a frame to maintain distance and prevent them from flattening you, creating space to re-pummel back to guard.

name: Pendulum (Leg Pummel) Guard Retention
description: Swing your free leg in a pendulum arc and re-pummel it to redirect your hips and re-establish your knee line in front of a passer circling toward your legs.

name: Knee Cut Pass Recovery
description: Stop the knee slice by framing on the passer's shoulder and hip while sliding your trapped knee out to re-insert it as a shield, recovering half or open guard.

name: Inverting to Retain Guard
description: When the passer back-steps or long-steps to spin toward your legs, invert by dropping your shoulders and lifting your hips to follow their rotation and keep your legs between you and them.

name: Leg Pummeling Guard Retention
description: Continuously re-pummel your legs back inside the passer's hip line whenever they try to clear them, re-entering a guard from which you can attack.

name: Octopus Guard
description: A modern attacking open guard where the bottom player comes up onto a hip, controls the far arm, and slides their head and shoulder under the opponent's arm to invade toward the back.

name: Octopus Guard Back Take
description: From octopus guard, drive your head and shoulder under the opponent's armpit, climb the back, and bring the second hook in to take back control.

name: Octopus Guard Sweep
description: From octopus guard, use the deep underarm and far-arm control to drive the opponent over your head and shoulder, coming up on top as they roll.

name: Buggy Choke
description: A defensive strangle from the bottom of side control or under mount: trap the opponent's near arm, thread your arm behind their neck, and lock a figure-four behind your own knee to finish a triangle-style choke from underneath.

name: The Rotolo Choke
description: A modern inverted strangle associated with Pedro Rotolo, entered from leg entanglements and back-exposure scrambles in the leg-lock game, threading an arm across the neck to finish from the inverted position.

name: Crab Ride
description: A modern back-attack control where you sit on the opponent's lower back facing their legs, hooking inside their thighs with your feet, feeding into the truck, back control, and leg entanglements.

name: Crab Ride to Back Take
description: From the crab ride, drop a hook inside the far thigh and rotate around the opponent's hip to insert both hooks and arrive at full back control.

name: Mikey Lock (Musumeci Footlock)
description: A rotational ankle-lock popularized by Mikey Musumeci using a deep instep wrap and a unique wrist position to attack the foot with rotation rather than a standard Achilles squeeze.

name: Butterfly Ashi
description: A hybrid entanglement blending a butterfly hook with an ashi garami leg knot, letting you elevate and off-balance for sweeps while threatening leg locks.

name: 2-on-1 Seated Guard
description: A modern seated open-guard system built around a two-hands-on-one-arm grip from the floor, using arm control to off-balance, arm-drag, and hunt the back or single-leg sweeps.

name: Marcelo Arm Drag to Back
description: Marcelo Garcia's arm-drag system from butterfly or seated guard: secure the wrist and tricep, drag the arm across the centerline, and climb to the back as the shoulder turns away.

name: Reverse De La Riva Heel Hook
description: An entry to an inside heel hook from reverse de la riva guard, using the RDLR hook to off-balance and load the opponent's near leg, then knotting into ashi to attack the heel.

name: Inside Sankaku Entry
description: A leg-knot entry to the inside-triangle (honey-hole) configuration, triangling your legs around the opponent's leg with the foot trapped inside to set up inside heel hooks.

name: Front Headlock to Back
description: From a front headlock off a failed shot or snap, spin to the side opposite the opponent's elbow and circle to the back or a rear bodylock.

name: Snap Down to Back
description: From standing, snap the opponent's head down with collar ties, break their posture forward, and circle to the back or a front-headlock-to-back transition.

name: Single Leg to the Back
description: Instead of completing the takedown, use single-leg control to run the pipe and circle behind the opponent for a back-take.

name: Shrug (Go-Behind)
description: From a collar tie or against a snap, shrug the opponent's arm and head over your shoulder and slip behind for a go-behind to the back or rear bodylock.

name: Rear Body Lock Takedown
description: After getting behind the opponent standing, lock a rear bodylock, then lift or trip them down while keeping the back.

name: Wrestle-Up to Single Leg
description: From seated guard, come up to your feet, capture a single leg, and finish a takedown or come up to top position.

name: K-Guard Back Take
description: From K-guard, instead of extending to a leg lock, use the under-leg frame to elevate and rotate around the hip, coming up to the back.

name: Osoto Gari (Outside Trip)
description: A major outside reap throw from the clinch where you step outside the opponent's leg and drive your leg backward into theirs while pulling their upper body forward to trip them to the mat.

name: Ouchi Gari (Inside Trip)
description: A major inside reap takedown from the clinch where you hook your leg behind the opponent's near leg and drive your weight through while controlling the upper body to take them down.

name: Kouchi Gari (Minor Inside Trip)
description: A quick inside foot sweep hooking the opponent's near heel and pulling it forward while pushing their upper body backward to off-balance them to the mat.

name: Uchi Mata (Inner Thigh Throw)
description: A powerful judo-derived throw driving your inner thigh into the opponent's inner thigh while wheeling them over your hip â€” one of the highest-percentage throws in competition.

name: Fireman's Carry
description: Duck under the opponent's arm, scoop their near arm and near leg, and roll them over your back to the mat in a single arching motion.

name: North-South Escape to Guard
description: From under north-south control, bridge and turn into the opponent while framing on the hips to create space, then shrimp and re-insert your legs to recover full guard.

name: No-Gi Baseball Choke
description: From side control or turtle, place both forearms across the opponent's throat â€” one blade pressing down on the near side, one pressing up from the far side â€” and squeeze to cut off blood flow. A powerful blood choke that needs no collar grip.

name: Crucifix Entry from Turtle
description: From the top of a turtled opponent, reach over and trap their near arm with your legs while securing their far arm with your hands, immobilizing both arms to establish the crucifix.

name: Leg Lock Defense â€” Re-Ashi Escape
description: Escape a heel hook or ankle lock by rotating your knee toward the attacker's body to clear the line of force, then re-pummel your leg inside to a safer position or disengage entirely.

name: Cross Collar Choke
description: From closed guard or mount, grip deep into both collars with a cross-grip and rotate the wrists to drive the forearm blades into the carotid arteries. The most fundamental gi choke.

name: Loop Choke
description: Grip the collar with one hand while posting the other forearm across the throat, then loop the collar under the chin as the opponent postures or passes, cutting off the carotid arteries with the lapel.

name: Bow and Arrow Choke
description: From back control, grip the collar with one hand and the far leg at the knee with the other, then extend the body like drawing a bow to crank the collar tight across the neck. One of the highest-percentage gi back attacks.

name: Clock Choke
description: From turtle top, drive one forearm across the throat using the collar grip while walking your feet around the opponent head clock-wise, using your body weight to crank the choke tight.

name: Baseball Bat Choke
description: From side control or knee on belly, grip both collars with staggered hands like holding a baseball bat and drive them across the throat to compress the carotids. Often set up when the opponent frames against the neck.

name: Paper Cutter Choke
description: From side control, feed the near collar to your bottom hand and use the top hand to drive the blade of the wrist across the throat in a slicing motion, compressing the carotid artery.

name: Brabo Choke (Gi)
description: Feed the opponent lapel under their arm and across their own neck, then close the arm triangle using the lapel as the choking surface rather than your own arm.

name: Collar Choke from Back
description: From back control, feed one hand deep under the chin to grip the far collar, then lock the second hand over the top for the cross-collar squeeze â€” a blood choke finishing alternative to the rear naked choke.

name: Spider Guard
description: Post both feet in the opponent biceps while gripping the sleeves, using the leg-arm connection to control posture, distance and angle for sweeps and submissions.

name: Lasso Guard
description: Thread one leg through the opponent arm and around the outside, wrapping the shin against their forearm while gripping the sleeve, creating strong rotation control for sweeps and omoplata entries.

name: Collar Sleeve Guard
description: Control one sleeve with both hands while one foot pushes the bicep and the other hooks the hip or ankle, using the collar-sleeve connection to manipulate posture and weight distribution.

name: Balloon Sweep
description: From closed guard, grip the collar and sleeve, place a foot on the hip, and use the collar pull combined with hip extension to flip the opponent over in a rotating motion.

name: Spider Guard Sweep
description: From spider guard, extend one leg to break the arm straight while pulling the sleeve and switching the other hook to the hip, toppling the opponent to the straightened-arm side.

name: Lasso Sweep
description: From lasso guard, use the rotational control of the lasso leg combined with the sleeve grip to off-balance the opponent and sweep them to the lasso side, coming up into a dominant position.

name: Lapel Guard
description: Extract the opponent lapel and thread it through their legs or around limbs to create entanglements that restrict movement, the foundation for worm guard, squid guard and various lapel-based sweeps.

name: Worm Guard
description: Thread the opponent lapel under their leg and back to your grip, creating a powerful leg and posture lock that severely restricts their passing and sets up off-balancing sweeps.

name: Squid Guard
description: An advanced lapel entanglement where the lapel is threaded around the arm and back, creating an omoplata-like shoulder control with the lapel while restricting the opponent posture and balance.

name: Choi Bar
description: A shoulder-and-arm lock attacked from open guard, swinging a leg over the head and trapping the arm to finish like a hybrid armbar/omoplata. We drilled this from De La Riva.

name: Choi Bar Entry (Open Guard)
description: Setting up the Choi Bar from open guard (e.g. De La Riva): off-balance the opponent, clear your hook through and swing your other leg over the head to lock the shoulder.

name: Shoulder Crunch
description: A compressing shoulder-lock control that traps the arm across the body and crunches the shoulder, opening up a chain of attacks. Popular in modern no-gi.

name: Scarf Hold (Kesa Gatame)
description: A side pin where you sit beside the opponent, head-and-arm trapped under your armpit while you control the far side. A heavy top control to attack from.

name: Scarf Hold Choke
description: A choke from the scarf hold (kesa gatame), using the trapped head-and-arm and your shoulder pressure to cut off the neck.

name: Reverse Buggy Choke
description: A reverse variation of the buggy choke, attacking the neck with your legs from the bottom when the opponent is in side control on the opposite side.

name: Suloev Stretch
description: A back-attack control that stretches the opponent by trapping a leg and extending the body, breaking their defensive posture to open up chokes and back retention.

name: Kipping Escape (Mount)
description: A fundamental mount escape: bridge explosively and kip your hips to bump the opponent forward, creating space to recover guard or come out the back.

name: F'Arce Choke
description: A modern D'Arce-family choke (one of Jeff Glover's named variations), threading the arm for a tight no-gi strangle from front headlock and turtle scrambles.

name: Grip Break
description: Fundamental gi skill: breaking the opponent's grips on your sleeves, collar and pants to free yourself and start your own offense.

name: Ezekiel Choke (Gi)
description: A choke using your own sleeve: feed one hand behind the neck, grip your other sleeve and saw the forearm across the throat. Classic from mount, also works from inside guard. Requires the gi.

name: Triangle from Open Guard
description: Locking up a triangle choke from open, spider or collar-sleeve guard by isolating one arm in and one arm out, then climbing the legs to finish.

name: Hip Escape (Shrimp)
description: The foundational solo movement: frame, bridge slightly and push off your feet to swing your hips away, creating space to recover guard or escape. Taught day one.

name: Technical Stand-Up
description: The fundamental way to stand up safely in base: post on one hand and the opposite foot, swing the trailing leg through and rise while staying protected. Core self-defense movement.

name: Rubber Guard
description: A high, flexible closed-guard system (10th Planet) where you use a hand to trap your own shin high on the opponent's back, breaking their posture to attack chokes and the gogoplata. No-gi.

name: Seoi Nage (Shoulder Throw)
description: A judo shoulder throw: turn in under the opponent's arm, load them across your back and rotate to throw them over your shoulder to the mat.

name: O Goshi (Hip Throw)
description: A fundamental judo hip throw: secure an over-the-back grip, load the opponent onto your hip and rotate to throw them over.

name: Sumi Gaeshi (Sacrifice Throw)
description: A sacrifice throw from a body-lock or underhook: sit back and use a hook to roll the opponent over you into a sweep or top position. Common from seated guard.
